_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel's confirmed, finally — national on-highway average spiked 33.8c to $5.13/gal for the week ending 7/20 (EIA, released 7/21) as the Iran/Strait of Hormuz fight resumed and blew past the Gulf, Midwest and West Coast alike. Update your fuel surcharge line NOW, that's real, five outlets agree on it. Everything else — dry van above contract, flatbed at record highs, Georgia reefer squeezing as Florida closes out — is still the same unverified-but-persistent trade-press story from the last three cycles; treat it as a talking point for holding your ask, not a number to quote back at a broker.

_sourcing.status: Diesel PROMOTED to LIVE this cycle — the 3-way contradiction from 07-21 resolved cleanly: five independent outlets now agree on $5.134/gal for week ending 2026-07-20 (EIA data, released 2026-07-21), and the Iran/Hormuz-escalation narrative won out over the de-escalation story. Spot/modality/lanes/commodityRates remain carried-forward — no clean corroboration this cycle either. See refreshBlockers for egress status.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE, confirmed 2026-07-28: $5.134/gal (rounded to $5.13) for the week ending 2026-07-20, per EIA data released 2026-07-21. Corroborated across FIVE independent sources with consistent figures and a consistent causal story (Iran/U.S. conflict resumed, Strait of Hormuz tension, oil-shortage fears): (1) AgriNews 'Fuel gauge for week ending July 20' — EIA-sourced, states diesel spiked 33.8c to $5.134, third-highest weekly increase in EIA history, prior week $4.796, year-ago $3.812; (2) FleetOwner 'Diesel fuel prices hit $5.13 as a result of the Iran conflict' — EIA data released 7/21, national average rose 34c to $5.134, regional breakdown given (Gulf Coast +40c to $4.942, Midwest +33c to $4.988, West Coast +33c to $5.877), up $1.322 YoY; (3) AAA Oregon/Idaho — 'Diesel Surpasses $5 Nationally'; (4) Yahoo Finance — 'Diesel hits $5 per gallon as pump prices resume climb'; (5) ABC News — 'Diesel prices top $5. Here's what it means for what you buy.' All five agree on the $5.13/$5.134 figure, the >$5 threshold, and the Iran-conflict driver — no internal contradictions this time (unlike 07-21's dueling headlines). This also retroactively confirms last cycle's $4.796 reading (week ending 7/13) was the correct one of the three candidates carried that week. Note: no primary eia.gov fetch was possible (still 403, see refreshBlockers) — this is 5-source secondary corroboration, not a primary-source read, but it clears the bar the last three cycles couldn't.

Not verified this cycle — DAT/SONAR WebFetch still blocked (403), and WebSearch summaries were again inconsistent (a synthesized 'DAT July 20 Trendlines' figure of $3.03/mi national van linehaul vs. a separately-cited $2.44/mi 'excluding fuel surcharge' figure, reconciled only by AI-guesswork about fuel-surcharge math, not a clean single reading). Not promoted.
_sourcing.modality: carried-forward from the app's Q2 2026 modality ranges. Not verified this cycle. Same directional trade-press signal persists (dry van above contract, flatbed at record high) but exact current figures are still not corroborating cleanly: national van spot cited at $3.03/mi (DAT 'July 20th Trendlines,' 3c above June avg) with a separately-derived $2.59-2.60/mi all-in estimate stitched together from a different fuel-surcharge snippet; Georgia outbound reefer cited flat at $2.44/mi for a month (DAT blog) which doesn't reconcile against the national reefer linehaul figures ($2.85/mi tied to the July 4 holiday week) surfaced in the same search batch — different lanes/metrics/weeks mixed together, not a like-for-like current number. None promoted.
_sourcing.commodityRates: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle.
_sourcing.lanes: carried-forward, unchanged. Not verified this cycle. WebSearch again surfaced Georgia/Florida reefer as the live Southeast story (DAT blog: 'Florida closes, Georgia opens at higher rates') with Georgia outbound reefer flat at ~$2.44/mi for the past month, ~5c/mi above last year, peach volumes down 30% YoY per USDA — real, current-sounding signal, but still not a clean match to a specific lane number in the existing lanes list, so not promoted.
_sourcing.blurb: rewritten this cycle to lead with the newly-confirmed diesel spike and its fuel-surcharge implication; rate-stance coaching (hold your ask) carried forward as before, explicitly flagged as unverified-but-persistent trade press rather than a fresh live read.
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: Same caveat as the last three cycles, still unresolved for spot/modality/lanes: trade press keeps saying dry van spot is above contract for the first time since Feb 2022, flatbed is at a record high, and Southeast reefer is tight (Florida closing, Georgia opening higher). Directionally consistent with the 'up' trend (reinforced this week by the confirmed diesel spike), but every attempt to pin an exact current spot/modality number has produced internally inconsistent or mismatched-metric WebSearch snippets. Do not put into numeric fields until a primary source (dat.com/trendlines or eia.gov) is actually reachable.

refreshBlockers: Re-tested egress first, as instructed: WebFetch/curl to eia.gov (both /petroleum/gasdiesel/ and /dnav/pet/pet_pri_gnd_dcus_nus_w.htm) returned CONNECT tunnel failed / HTTP 403 again today — block is unchanged from the 07-07, 07-14 and 07-21 attempts (destination-side 403 via the agent proxy, not a proxy outage). WebSearch works and this cycle it was enough to resolve the diesel contradiction from last week: five independent outlets (AgriNews, FleetOwner, AAA, Yahoo Finance, ABC News) now agree on $5.134/gal for the week ending 2026-07-20, EIA data released 2026-07-21, driven by resumed Iran/Strait-of-Hormuz fighting — clean enough to promote to LIVE and advance asOf to 2026-07-21. Spot/modality/lanes searches this cycle were still not clean: figures mixed different weeks, lanes, and fuel-surcharge-inclusive-vs-exclusive metrics without a single reconciled current reading (see modality/spotAllIn/lanes notes), so those stayed carried-forward — asOf was NOT advanced on their account, only on diesel's. Broader web-fetch access (not just search) to a primary source like eia.gov or dat.com/trendlines would let spot/modality get the same clean-primary-source treatment diesel just got, instead of waiting for enough secondary outlets to independently agree.
